note: Agent Plasticity (arXiv 2610.08902v1, 2026-10-06). Headline numbers on screen: 73.3% (Claude Fable 5, Hard chess held-out ID, average of checkpoints 16-20), 98% (GPT-5.6 Luna, relevant chess decisions without artifact use, pooled Hard + Easy), 298 (GPT-5.6 Sol Psat) and 57 (Claude Fable 5 Psat). Psat is an estimated saturation-fit efficiency in percentage points per $1,000 of mean per-game learning cost on the combined chess+Go+Hex curve; it depends on the protocol and provider pricing. All results are the authors' own runs.

numbers.73.3: Claude Fable 5, Hard chess held-out ID score, averaged over checkpoints 16-20 (sec 3.2, p. 6); an absolute measured score

claims.l01: Abstract and Finding 2 (p. 7-8): Claude Fable 5 reaches the highest fitted endpoint while GPT-5.6 Sol has the highest estimated plasticity; 'the agent that ultimately performs best need not be the one that improves most efficiently.'
claims.l02: Sec 1: most agent evaluations ask what an agent can accomplish at a fixed point in time; agents can also learn from experience.
claims.l03: Sec 2.1: model weights remain frozen; each acting episode begins in a fresh context; future instances inherit tools, skills, strategies and textual memory (artifacts).
claims.l04: Sec 3.1 and App. B: Chess, Go, Hex and NetHack; between checkpoints the same model reflects on training trajectories and feedback and proposes artifact revisions.
claims.l05: Sec 2.2: agent plasticity is held-out performance gain per unit learning cost, reported in score points per $1,000.
claims.l08: Sec 3.2 (p. 6): Claude Fable 5's Hard chess held-out ID score averages 73.3% over checkpoints 16-20.
claims.l09: Sec 3.5 (p. 8): GPT-5.6 Luna takes about 98% of relevant decisions without artifact use, pooled over Hard and Easy chess.
claims.l10: Sec 3.4 (p. 7): GPT-5.6 Sol has the highest estimated Psat at 298 percentage points per $1,000 of mean per-game learning cost. Receipt crop.
claims.l11: Sec 3.4 (p. 7): Claude Fable 5's Psat is 57 and it reaches the highest fitted performance level; endpoint capability and acquisition efficiency differ (Finding 2).
claims.l13: Sec 3.5 (p. 9): in one GPT-5.5 run the reflection step keeps telling the agent to load its saved move-picking program right away, yet the agent still spends its first steps listing and reading files.
claims.l14: Sec 3.4 (p. 7): 'we interpret plasticity as a protocol-dependent measure, not a universal model ranking'; sec 4 (p. 10-11): estimates depend on score headroom, the learning horizon, saturation-fit assumptions, and provider pricing.
claims.l15: Summary line; adds no new claim.
